title: What If You Were Shrunk Inside Your Own Body?

lines.text: You've been shrunk smaller than a blood cell... and your own body is about to attack you.
That squishy cushion under you? One red blood cell.
A single drop of your blood holds millions of them.
Hear that thumping? That's your heart... and you're heading straight in.
Every beat, the valves behind you slam shut. That lub-dub? That's them closing.
One squeeze fires you into your lungs... into tunnels so tight, blood cells barely squeeze through.
And through a wall over a hundred times thinner than paper, oxygen floods in... and carbon dioxide drifts out. That's the air you breathe out.
A neutrophil. Your body's first responder. To it, you're not you... you're an intruder. And it swallows intruders whole.
The current drags you back to your heart, and its main pump launches you into the biggest artery you have!
You survived. But somewhere in your lungs... a white blood cell is still trying to digest your shoe.
